Diagnosis.Cancer Type: Adenocarcinoma the tail of the pancreas
Diagnosis.Molecular Markers: VUS seen in AXIN1, CTC1, ERCC4, MC1R

Additional Comments: The patient is a 68-year-old woman with adenocarcinoma of the tail of the pancreas, which has extended to the posterior gastric wall and possibly invaded the left adrenal gland, causing occlusion of the splenic vein. She has been treated with gemcitabine and Abraxane, initially on a standard schedule but later adjusted to an alternate week schedule due to neutropenia. She has tolerated the adjusted schedule well and has completed 4 full cycles. She experiences no cancer pain but uses oxycodone for chronic back and shoulder pain. Her appetite fluctuates, but her weight remains stable, and she denies symptoms of neuropathy. She has a facial rash that is tolerable and has been seen by a gynecologic oncologist regarding a likely benign right adnexal mass. Germ line testing revealed no pathologic variants, with VUS seen in AXIN1, CTC1, ERCC4, and MC1R. She has a history of hepatitis C, successfully treated, hypertension, and renal lithiasis, and her ECOG performance status is 1.
